Comments (English): As our family grew, the amount of dishes to wash each day increased significantly. In the past, hand washing was sufficient, but after the family expanded, a single meal would leave a huge pile of dishes, cups, and cutlery, making the time spent washing dishes feel burdensome. After much consideration, I decided to purchase the Samsung Electronics BESPOKE AI Built-in Hot Air Dryer Dishwasher (14-place setting). After using it for a few weeks, I am generally very satisfied with the product. Its biggest advantage is, of course, the ample storage capacity. Perhaps because it is a 14-place setting model, I can fit dishes, pots, and pans from a meal all in one go, so there is almost no need to run it in separate batches. It was especially convenient on weekends when the whole family gathers for a meal; even though the amount of dishes increases significantly, there is still plenty of room for storage. The cleaning performance is also satisfactory. Even greasy plates and dishes with liquid stains were cleaned thoroughly, and I felt that the dishes were being kept more hygienic than when washing by hand. The hot air drying function was also more satisfying than expected; it dried well, leaving minimal water stains, and allowed for immediate storage, which was very convenient. I was also impressed by the AI features that adjust the washing process according to usage patterns. It is intuitive and easy to operate, so even first-time users could adapt easily. True to BESPOKE's reputation, the design is clean and luxurious, blending well with my kitchen interior. However, it isn't without its drawbacks. The initial cost of remodeling the sink and the price of the product might feel a bit burdensome. Also, using the dishwasher efficiently requires a knack for arranging dishes in the proper places, and I experienced some trial and error at first as I wasn't used to it. Nevertheless, considering the time and effort I used to spend on washing dishes, I believe it is a sufficiently satisfying investment. In particular, for households like mine where the number of family members has increased and the amount of dishwashing has grown, this product can definitely improve the quality of life. I sigh less often looking at piles of dishes after meals, and I now spend more time with my family. Overall, I am satisfied with the cleaning power, drying performance, capacity, and design, so I think it is a dishwasher worth recommending.

Comments (English): [ Lots of Features, Quiet and Smooth Installation ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher that was in our home when we bought it, failed after almost 20 years of service. We then began our search, we wanted to buy from Costco because of Return Policy, extra Warranty and included Install/Haul Away, etc.Started with Consumer Reports Ratings/Reviews and crossed to the models Costco offered. Within our price "cap" and had features we wanted. That brought us to this LG Model. I will add we've had an LG Refrigerator for 15 plus year with zero problems, which helped us decide.We like the cleaning modes and options offered and all dishes have come out clean with no issues. The Interior "tub" lights help more that we would have first thought. The rack layouts have handled all our dishes and with just the two of us we do two loads a week. the door popping open to add drying, is helpful too. Enjoy the much quieter washer over the one it replaced! At first the Phone App to manage the washer seemed silly but have come to enjoy it. Hopefully won't need it but being able to get full diagnostics via the App can save time too. Still early in the ownership "curve" but very happy so far with how things have been with our new dishwasher! Installation:I want to add this as in reading many Costco Reviews, it seemed 70% of the "One Star" related to Installation issues not the actual dishwasher performance itself. Needless to say this made me concerned about the Installation.We made a point to fully go over Costco Installation Requirements to avoid the Installation Day "surprises" .We had a plumber come out as we were aware of an "odd" thing done when our house was built and had to have the Water Valve replaced. Then had an electrician update our dedicated Circuit Breaker(our washer is hardwired) with one rated as GFCI. I then measured the Opening three times to confirm our LG Model(from online documentation) would fit in the existing opening. Once all that was done, we placed the order.We live in Clark County, WA and give praise to Edwardo and his partner from Transmotion! They called to say they'd be early(fine with us). I was given a chance to inspect the washer for scratches or dents(all was fine). I pointed out the new Water Valve and GFCI Breaker to them and since we'd already removed the old washer, they were done in 40 minutes after giving us a preview of features and watching a test run. I later got an email from Transmotion with a full set of pictures thy had taken at steps of the Installation as well. I think they appreciated us also having everything ready when they arrived.

Sentence (English): The biggest reason I applied for the Care Service while using the LG DIOS Objet Collection Dishwasher DUE6BGE was my anxiety about hygiene.
Comments (English): The biggest reason I applied for the Care Service while using the LG DIOS Objet Collection Dishwasher DUE6BGE was my anxiety about hygiene. Since a dishwasher is a product used every day, I was constantly bothered by the fact that even if it looks clean on the outside, it is difficult to personally verify the internal condition or whether it is being properly maintained. Before receiving the service, I thought that simply adding detergent and running it would make it clean, but as time passed, I realized that it is difficult for a user to inspect internal maintenance, nozzles, or filter conditions. So, I decided to apply for the LG Care Service to get a proper inspection and maintenance. The difference before and after the service was more significant than I expected. Before the service, I was in a vague state of thinking, "It's running well, so there shouldn't be any problems," but after the service, I gained a definite sense of security knowing that the interior was also being maintained. I felt that not only the exterior but also the unseen parts were inspected and managed, allowing me to use the product with much greater peace of mind. In particular, the process of the Care Manager visiting to inspect the internal condition, clean it, and check its overall state instilled a sense of trust. Because it checks even the details users might easily overlook, I strongly felt that it was a product being professionally cared for rather than one managed on my own. The advantages are, of course, reduced anxiety about hygiene and the ability to use the product with peace of mind for a longer period. Furthermore, the fact that it is maintained regularly gave me confidence that it would help preserve the product's performance. The only downsides are that scheduling a visit is required and it is not a service that can be received immediately at a desired time. However, considering the overall satisfaction, I felt this was a perfectly acceptable trade-off. Since a dishwasher is a product used every day, I was constantly bothered by the fact that even if it looks clean on the outside, it is difficult to personally verify the internal condition or whether it is being properly maintained. Before receiving the service, I thought that simply adding detergent and running it would make it clean, but as time passed, I realized that it is difficult for a user to inspect internal maintenance, nozzles, or filter conditions. So, I decided to apply for the LG Care Service to get a proper inspection and maintenance. The difference before and after the service was more significant than I expected. Before the service, I was in a vague state of thinking, "It's running well, so there shouldn't be any problems," but after the service, I gained a definite sense of security knowing that the interior was also being maintained. I felt that not only the exterior but also the unseen parts were inspected and managed, allowing me to use the product with much greater peace of mind. In particular, the process of the Care Manager visiting to inspect the internal condition, clean it, and check its overall state instilled a sense of trust. Because it checks even the details users might easily overlook, I strongly felt that it was a product being professionally cared for rather than one managed on my own. The advantages are, of course, reduced anxiety about hygiene and the ability to use the product with peace of mind for a longer period. Furthermore, the fact that it is maintained regularly gave me confidence that it would help preserve the product's performance. The only downsides are that scheduling a visit is required and it is not a service that can be received immediately at a desired time. However, considering the overall satisfaction, I felt this was a perfectly acceptable trade-off. Ultimately, the LG Care service felt more than just a simple inspection; it strongly felt like a management system that allows you to continue using the product with confidence. I believe it is a highly satisfying service for those who use their dishwashers for a long time and prioritize hygiene.

Sentence (English): I bought this to replace an older Frigidaire that was no longer getting dishes clean, I believe the pump was going bad.
Comments (English): [ Not what I was hoping for ] || ---------------- || I bought this to replace an older Frigidaire that was no longer getting dishes clean, I believe the pump was going bad. Based on Consumer Reports ratings and reviews I expected good performance out of this LG dishwasher. Installing it was simple enough, looks great in the kitchen. Runs extremely quiet. However that is very secondary to the primary factor: How does it perform washing dishes? For me the answer to that question is unfortunatley, less than satisfactory. If there's any significant or dried food soil on the dishes, they do not come out clean. instead there's a dried streaky film on them. Sometimes bits of dried food soil. Even on the lower rack where I'd expect dishes get the maximum washing action from the spray arms, dishes can come through the wash process with a film on them. Even with selecting the high temp wash option that raises water temp and extends the wash cycle. The only solution to this is to completely wash/wipe them with a dishcloth before I load them into the machine. And that defeats the purpose of having a dishwasher in the first place. My expectation of a good dishwasher is: I can rinse the dishes in hot water as I load them to remove most of the soil, and the dishwasher should be able to handle the rest. Unfortunately this machine does not perform to that degree. Instead I get a soil film on some of the dishes unless I make sure they go into the machine spotless. I could have kept my old dishwasher, saved hundreds of dollars, and gotten the same result. Sorry, but I am not satisfied with this dishwasher and cannot recommend it to others for purchase. Dissapointing.

Sentence (English): I am leaving a review because I am truly satisfied after using the Samsung Electronics BESPOKE AI Built-in Hot Air Dryer Dishwasher (14-place setting).
Comments (English): I am leaving a review because I am truly satisfied after using the Samsung Electronics BESPOKE AI Built-in Hot Air Dryer Dishwasher (14-place setting). Previously, having dishes pile up several times a day was one of the most difficult household chores, but since using this dishwasher, I have definitely gained more breathing room in the kitchen. Especially since we have children, we use a lot of dishes, and the 14-place setting is incredibly convenient as I can load a large amount at once. The feature I like most is definitely the hot air drying function. With the products I used before, water would often remain after washing, requiring me to wipe them again, but this product finishes drying cleanly after washing, allowing me to store them immediately. I am also satisfied that dishes prone to water droplets, such as glass cups and plastic containers, come out much drier and fresher. I also really love the built-in design. It blends naturally with the kitchen furniture, creating a clean and luxurious atmosphere without looking like it sticks out after installation. True to the BESPOKE line, the design is beautiful; it doesn't detract from the kitchen interior but actually looks even more sophisticated. It is also more intuitive and easier to use than I expected. You just put the dishes in and select a course, and it handles everything from washing to drying automatically, so I can use it without any hassle even on busy days. The operating noise isn't loud, so I didn't mind running it in the evening. Most importantly, it uses less water than washing by hand, and the cleaning power is excellent, so I am highly satisfied with the hygiene aspect. It cleans greasy frying pans and dishes stained with sauce thoroughly, saving me time that I used to spend handwashing every time. At first, I wondered if a dishwasher was really necessary, but after using it, I find myself wishing I had bought it sooner. I believe it is a product that reduces the time spent in the kitchen and increases the time spent with family. Sentence (English): I purchased this because the amount of dishes increased with the arrival of children, and I am truly satisfied.
Comments (English): [ It was comfortable ^^ ] || ---------------- || I purchased this because the amount of dishes increased with the arrival of children, and I am truly satisfied. Since my kitchen isn't very spacious, I chose a countertop dishwasher; installation was easier than I expected, and the Bespoke design blends well with the kitchen's atmosphere. In particular, being able to load all the dishes piled up after meals at once has drastically reduced my dishwashing time. As it is a 6-place setting model, it fits dishes for a family of four comfortably, and it is convenient to be able to wash pots and cooking utensils along with the dishes. The cleaning power was also satisfactory. Even greasy dishes and children's snack plates are cleaned thoroughly, and thanks to the high-temperature sterilization and drying functions, I feel reassured knowing I can use it hygienically. The noise level isn't high either, so running it in the evening wasn't a burden. ^^ I feel liberated from the daily chore of washing dishes, and my quality of life has improved. I especially recommend this product to newlyweds, families raising children, and families of 2 to 4 people.

Sentence (English): As a working couple, seeing the pile of dishes accumulate every evening was a subtle source of stress.
Comments (English): As a working couple, seeing the pile of dishes accumulate every evening was a subtle source of stress. Especially when preparing meals for a family of three—including a child—the sink would quickly fill up with dishes and pots. When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. Comments (English): As a working couple, seeing the pile of dishes accumulate every evening was a subtle source of stress. Especially when preparing meals for a family of three—including a child—the sink would quickly fill up with dishes and pots. When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. If you desire a clean kitchen interior, want to be completely free from dishwashing stress, or are a family concerned about hygiene with children, I highly recommend choosing this LG Objet Collection 14-place setting dishwasher without hesitation. It truly changes your quality of life!

When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. If you desire a clean kitchen interior, want to be completely free from dishwashing stress, or are a family concerned about hygiene with children, I highly recommend choosing this LG Objet Collection 14-place setting dishwasher without hesitation. It truly changes your quality of life!

Comments (English): As a working couple, seeing the pile of dishes accumulate every evening was a subtle source of stress. Especially when preparing meals for a family of three—including a child—the sink would quickly fill up with dishes and pots. When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. If you desire a clean kitchen interior, want to be completely free from dishwashing stress, or are a family concerned about hygiene with children, I highly recommend choosing this LG Objet Collection 14-place setting dishwasher without hesitation. It truly changes your quality of life!

Comments (English): As a working couple, seeing the pile of dishes accumulate every evening was a subtle source of stress. Especially when preparing meals for a family of three—including a child—the sink would quickly fill up with dishes and pots. When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. If you desire a clean kitchen interior, want to be completely free from dishwashing stress, or are a family concerned about hygiene with children, I highly recommend choosing this LG Objet Collection 14-place setting dishwasher without hesitation. It truly changes your quality of life!

When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. If you desire a clean kitchen interior, want to be completely free from dishwashing stress, or are a family concerned about hygiene with children, I highly recommend choosing this LG Objet Collection 14-place setting dishwasher without hesitation. It truly changes your quality of life!

Especially when preparing meals for a family of three—including a child—the sink would quickly fill up with dishes and pots. When I completely renovated my kitchen, I put a dishwasher at the very top of my list of essential appliances to improve my quality of life. After comparing various brands and models, I chose the LG Electronics Objet Collection dishwasher because I was completely satisfied with both its features and design. It truly is the number one most satisfying appliance I have purchased this year. First of all, from an interior design perspective, the design is superb. It is built-in so cleanly that it looks like one with the subtle warm tones of the base cabinets and the sophisticated tile floor. It fits perfectly without any parts sticking out beyond the sink line, making the kitchen look much more modern and spacious. The luxurious and soft hue characteristic of the Nature Beige color makes the overall atmosphere of the kitchen even cozier. I am now truly realizing why everyone says the Objet Collection completes the interior. What is most impressive, however, is its overwhelming capacity and cleaning power. At first, I was worried it might be too big for a family of three, but after actually using it, I realized that bigger is always better. It fits everything at once—from basic dishes like rice and soup bowls to large frying pans and cutting boards used for cooking—making it perfect for doing a day's worth of dishes all at once. The height of the inner basket is freely adjustable, so you can easily arrange bulky cooking utensils without any stress. The washing and drying performance exceeds expectations and is truly a whole new world. Thanks to the 100% TrueSteam function, even a frying pan heavily stained with grease comes out squeaky clean, looking like a brand new dish, simply by putting it in without pre-washing. Since high-temperature steam sterilizes 99.999% of harmful bacteria and viruses, I feel safe washing children's dishes and cutlery, which gives me great peace of mind as a parent. The drying function is also excellent. Since hot air drying is performed simultaneously, even the tops of plastic containers and cups, where moisture tends to linger, are completely dry. Once the wash cycle is finished, the door opens automatically to vent out any odors and residual steam, ensuring a clean finish without worrying about stubborn smells. If you run it overnight and open it in the morning, the dishes are perfectly dry, ready to be put away in the cupboard immediately. The noise level is as quiet as a library, so it is not at all bothersome even if you are watching TV in the living room or running it late at night. Its Grade 1 energy efficiency rating is also a major draw, as it keeps electricity bills low even if you run it every day. Since household chores have been drastically reduced, I now have the luxury to fully converse with my family or relax after dinner. If you desire a clean kitchen interior, want to be completely free from dishwashing stress, or are a family concerned about hygiene with children, I highly recommend choosing this LG Objet Collection 14-place setting dishwasher without hesitation. It truly changes your quality of life!

Sentence (English): Do not buy this!
Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY! Beyond disappointed. ] || ---------------- || Do not buy this! Purchased in Dec 2024. Was on backorder so it wasn't delivered until mid/late January. Took a couple of months to get my plumber scheduled to install. Should have kept the GE I bought 18 years ago at Goodwill for $25. A few months ago, it started leaving black greasy sludge and little black specks on my dishes. Most of it shows up on the top rack, but I've found on some silverware in top rack and on dishes on the bottom rack too. From everything I've read, that usually means something is circulating through the wash system instead of just settling in the bottom. And internal. nothing I can troubleshoot and fix! After immense (hours) of research and troubleshooting AI says these are likely the issue:. 1. Debris/sludge trapped in the sump or chopper area below the filters (most likely) . 2. Partial restriction somewhere in the wash/drain system causing old residue to recirculate. 3. Deteriorating internal component (less likely because you also have greasy slime) . The filter and sump area collect a lot of this black gunk — enough that I've filled multiple paper towels each time trying to clean it out. I have photos. The bottom and lower sides of the dishwasher get coated in it, and it takes several rounds of wiping to get it off. I've repeatedly cleaned the removable filters, scrubbed the sump with hot water and Dawn, removed standing water, and used the cleaning products Whirlpool recommends (and a few others I tried out of desperation). No matter what I do, the problem keeps coming back. I have done recommended trouble shooting 3 times now over past several months. but now "your warranty has run out" and without paying the ridiculous money I was just quoted for fixes, "sorry, but you are out of warranty and nothing we can do! " She went right into this sales pitch! And personality changed when I expressed this was ridiculous. I asked for customer service email to voice my concerns/complaint to which I was told “I don't have that. You can google and find it yourself.” Well ain't that nice? I'll just goggle and find places to share DO NOT BUY instead! I've tried several different detergents, including ones recommended for Whirlpool machines. The dishwasher worked beautifully for months before this started, and nothing changed on my end — same water, same plumbing, same habits. I scrape food well, wipe grease into the trash, and don't have a garbage disposal attached. The drain hose looks fine, and dishes dry normally… they just come out with black specks and goo on them, which is disheartening to say the least. I'm an older gal with some knee and back issues, so doing these deep cleanings over and over has been tough. I've done the whole “YouTube cleaning routine” three times now — scooping water out, wiping down the inside, cleaning the spray arm, all of it. I can't keep doing this nor should I have to. I'm on a limited income, and I really don't have the budget to pay for repairs on a dishwasher that's barely a year old I've only used 12-14ish months! I've bragged on this dishwasher to friends and folks online and 1 or 2 i think have purchased — stupid me! My final decision to buy your Whirlpool was because so many of your appliances are made right near me in Kinston. Just called customer service (where I was put on hold for FORTY minutes before someone came on the call to "help" me). with choice AA of a $36ish/month fee with current 10% discount! Woopies! or one time fee that was something like $344! INSANE. Beware if you buy this. Had I contacted them when the problem started I'd have been in their warranty window, but because stupid me has been attempting troubleshooting instead, they won't help me. From my research, it appears this is something internally malfunctioning I can't fix! Should have kept the $25 Goodwill GE I had for 18 years, or chose the GE I was considering along with this one. Now, I just don't have in the budget to pay to fix a barely year old malfunctioning dishwasher! Beyond disappointing in the American made and possibly NC made thing! #Disgusted! My only recourse is to tell the world. You've been warned. Trying to attach images but drop down box won't work.

Sentence (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Sentence (English): To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Sentence (English): First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Sentence (English): I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Sentence (English): While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Sentence (English): It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.
