Sentence (English): I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used.
Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Comments (English): Perhaps because this product is so popular, there was a huge backlog of deliveries and installations. It took four days after I ordered to get it installed. When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

When the unit arrived, I thought, "Ah, it's really big." To be honest, I bought it expecting it to be very convenient, but there are far more inconveniences than I anticipated. Since the reviews were all positive, I purchased it with high expectations that I would be able to use it well, but now that I’ve actually used it, I wonder if others find it really inconvenient. First of all, using the standard mode and high-temperature sterilization takes 2 hours and 1 minute, and even after running powerful drying, there is still a lot of water. So, I have to take the dishes out one by one, wipe them down with a dry cloth, and put them back in the cabinet. Also, there is so much water inside the dishwasher that I have to take all the dishes out, wipe the entire interior with a dry cloth, and wipe the drain hole down as well. As a result, it takes over an hour to clean and organize everything, including the dishes and the interior. I finally understand why previous users mentioned that the dishwasher emits a musty smell after a while. I realized that if you just leave dishes sitting around after using the dishwasher, the water gets trapped and stagnates, making odors inevitable. I’ve only used it twice so far, but managing it is more inconvenient and time-consuming than it is convenient. While the amount of water used is certainly small, I bought it primarily for sterilization, cleanliness, and convenience, but in reality, it requires too much effort and is quite inconvenient. And most importantly, it is difficult to fit dishes other than plates or small bowls. It is a chore to organize washable items one by one inside the dishwasher to maximize space, and it is also difficult to find room for rice bowls or soup bowls. I feel like it is a dishwasher designed solely for plates. Consequently, items like Lock & Lock airtight containers are a bit awkward to handle, and I have the hassle of having to hand-wash all the kitchen utensils and containers used while cooking separately. It really is true that it can only wash dishes (only plates), though not everything. Am I the only one experiencing this? Do others really find it easy to use? It seems like a product designed only for conveniently washing plates and cutlery. I honestly had no idea that this is how a product is supposed to be used. Because I have severe germophobia and a compulsion to wipe away over 95% of the moisture every time, I didn't realize before purchasing this that I would get this exhausted after just two uses. I do this because I simply cannot leave it wet, but to think I have to do this every day... Do others also just use it with moisture on? I was so curious that I asked the manufacturer, and they said it is normal for it to be damp. I thought that with the powerful drying function, it would be completely dry and fluffy, but that was not the case at all. I'm not sure if it's because I'm still a beginner and lack the knack, but I am writing down my honest thoughts after using it.

Comments (English): [ Overpriced and Underwhelming ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher replaced a noisy but well loved, 34 year old Maytag, which I would have fixed, but a pump gasket was nowhere to be found. Below is a comparison: On the plus side, the Kitchenaid is much quieter, mostly nearly silent. But, the 3-4 hour cycles are ridiculously long. Cleaning is comparable or a bit better, but there is no drying fan, and even on the "Pro Dry" setting, some items are still damp and the tub is quite wet. We've used cheap gel detergent with good results. The whole build is flimsy, apparently to reduce costs and shipping weight. Lots of thin plastic and thin metal. There's no way it will last as long as the old one. The door opens too stiffly and swings too low for such a frequently used item. The silverware carrier should be in front and on the second rack for ease of access. The drawer slides don't feel sturdy or smooth, and the third rack is mostly pointless. Despite some adjustability, the tines are too low and awkwardly placed and shaped for many items. I limited our choices to only machines that have a self cleaning filter like our old one. I didn't need a new, unwelcome and fussy filter cleaning chore. The towel bar handle makes opening and closing easy on old hands, but the buttons and display on the top edge were much too easy to accidentally hit - a constant annoyance. While the remaining time indicator is a plus, our countertop made it difficult to see without having to install the machine lower and further out than I would have otherwise liked. The installation, which, like the old machine, I did myself, was miserable. The included instructions were minimal, confusing, incomplete and left out many steps. An expensive machine like this should have come with a complete, printed instruction manual. After some hunting, I found one online, but it wasn't very good either. I needed to buy $30 worth of hose and fittings, since nothing was included and my old hardware didn't match. Routing of the wires and hoses was tight and not intuitive. Finally, Lowes' 48 hour return policy is a new low in customer support. They are far more interested in giving you a discount for opening a new credit account so they can harvest your data and payments. Instead of real customer friendly policies, you get nagging e-mails for costly extended but limited warranties. KitchenAid wants your data too, in exchange for equally limited warranty extensions. The dishwasher is just okay so far, but the purchasing, installation, documentation, quality and customer support have been miserable. It appears to be a race to the bottom. So much for competition.

Sentence (English): As I recently moved, I discarded my old dishwasher and purchased a new Samsung BESPOKE AI Built-in 14-place setting dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ A dishwasher that is the most satisfying in terms of design, color, and performance. ] || ---------------- || As I recently moved, I discarded my old dishwasher and purchased a new Samsung BESPOKE AI Built-in 14-place setting dishwasher. I completely replaced my kitchen sink while remodeling my home, and I am very satisfied because I feel I chose a product that matches perfectly. I have been using it for about two weeks now, and I am very happy with it as I have experienced no inconvenience in terms of performance. ## Clean design without handles or front buttons ##. The biggest reason I chose this product was the design of the front. While there are countless dishwashers with similar shapes, this Samsung model features a truly clean, single surface on the front, completely devoid of handles or buttons. Given the current trend favoring built-in appliances, I really like the clean design, which makes it difficult to tell whether it is a dishwasher or a kitchen sink base cabinet. ## Samsung's Cota White color ##. I really love Samsung Electronics' Cota White color. Nowadays, the standard sinks and refrigerator cabinets in newly built apartments mostly match well with the Cota White color. Although I only purchased the dishwasher this time, I think the kitchen would look incredibly neat and beautiful if I matched the regular refrigerator and kimchi refrigerator in the Cotta White color as well. ## Optimal AI Mode Courses and Hot Air Drying ##. As expected of a modern new product, it features a wide variety of modes. Water temperature and washing times vary depending on the mode, but generally, using just the AI mode seems sufficient. According to the installer, they recommend the AI mode for household use because higher hot water temperatures result in higher electricity bills. They also mentioned that the hot air drying function doesn't generate heat but rather blows out residual warmth, so it doesn't consume much electricity even when used for extended periods. That is why I use the AI mode with the hot air drying cycle set to a longer duration. ## Ample Storage and Cleaning Power ##. It is a 14-place setting model featuring three internal shelves. Even within the three shelves, there are many structures that allow the trays to be positioned upright or laid flat. Sentence (English): We wanted to try a different brand so we switched up from GE to this Whirlpool based on reviews, pictures, and price comparisons.
Comments (English): [ Huge Disappointment! ] || ---------------- || We wanted to try a different brand so we switched up from GE to this Whirlpool based on reviews, pictures, and price comparisons. What a huge disappointment and waste of good money! Make sure you go into a store to physically inspect your appliances, etc. before you buy them, big mistake on my part but I couldn't make it to the store, unfortunately.1) It does NOT dry the dishes, or the interior of the dw, no matter the extra heat settings. You might as well leave the heated dry off and dry the dishes yourself to save on energy! Very disappointing! 2) The pictures are misleading as far as the upper and lower racks and interior space. The top rack isn't wide enough to fit larger mugs, bowls, etc. and the lower rack has too big a space between the tines so certain dishes fall over and don't get washed as well as they should.3) There could be 6" more length to both the racks giving more space for more dishes. This is almost like a doll house dishwasher as far as I am concerned. I cook 95% of our meals here at home, and there isn't really enough space to do a full load as there was in our GE. Now I have to do 1-1/2 loads to the GE one. I use pots, pans, and more dishes than just a few plates, cups and silverware! 4) It washes dishes ok, but sometimes won't restart if you open it midstream and hit "resume" - you think the dishes are clean but find out later that it didn't actually resume and you have to re-run the dishwasher a full cycle to get them clean (but not dry, it doesn't do that like I wrote earlier)! It is easy to operate, and the noise level is manageable, but if you can't fit everything in there as I could with my old 24" GE, and it doesn't dry at all, what's even the point of rating it anything but a one star? We have and are almost satisfied with our Whirlpool clothes washer and dryer and decided we'd give their kitchen appliances a chance, but we wouldn't recommend them after this experience!

Of course, large pots, pans, and cutting boards still need to be hand-washed separately, but the fact that I can handle small dishes, cups, and baby tableware all at once has drastically reduced my housework time. However, stacking the dishes neatly requires a bit of knack, so it does take some time to get used to it. Cleaning power and the food strainer. The cleaning performance is also better than expected. Large food scraps are filtered out by the bottom strainer, while small pieces are flushed out directly through the drain hose using strong water pressure, making it very hygienic. Connecting to an outlet and water supply is essential, and the drain hose goes directly into the sink; I liked that maintenance wasn't as complicated as I thought. It is so satisfying to see the dishes squeaky clean thanks to the high-temperature washing. Neat installation service tailored for rental homes. Since we couldn't drill a hole in the kitchen countertop, we utilized the opening on the opposite side of the water purifier to run the water supply pipe. We also used a power strip to run the outlet from the water purifier, and the Samsung installers did such a neat job organizing even the exposed wires that it looks great aesthetically. Thanks to the professional touch, the wiring issues I was worried about were completely resolved. I am very satisfied with the clean finish. Overall review: For those who hesitated to install a dishwasher because they don't own their home, the countertop model seems like the best alternative. If you can somehow manage the water supply connection, I highly recommend installing it without hesitation. I am so happy that I can play with my child more instead of doing the dishes. Sentence (English): I initially planned to buy a built-in model, but I changed my mind after reading other people's reviews.
Comments (English): I initially planned to buy a built-in model, but I changed my mind after reading other people's reviews. The biggest advantage is being able to wash dishes immediately. I wanted a large size because I needed to wash pots and pans. Some reviews mentioned that built-in dishwashers wait until the dishes pile up before running, and that it is inconvenient to stand up after crouching down. Now that I am using the 5-6 place setting, I feel like I made the right choice. My family of four uses it very well twice a day, in the morning and evening. It is a really smart appliance, and I keep recommending it to everyone around me!

Sentence (English): We purchased this Maytag dishwasher for ~$1000 and had it installed.
Comments (English): [ Cleans well but noisy. First unit was a lemon. ] || ---------------- || We purchased this Maytag dishwasher for ~$1000 and had it installed. On its initial wash cycle, we noticed that the wash pump was very loud and constant. Peak decibel readings were around 55. We contacted Maytag and waited for a technician to come out. He said he would have to replace the pump so we went back to Home Depot to ask for a new unit. Be careful: Home Depot indicates that there are no returns on major appliances (including dishwashers) and Maytag will only honor a return if you purchase through them. Lucky for us, Home Depot said that they would give us a new unit which was eventually installed about 12 days later. The new unit is still louder than their rated dB level (we measured ~50 consistently) so we just run it at night. It does clean well and the third rack is great. Just not impressed with the noise level.

Sentence (English): After my trusted Bosch dishwasher gave out after 22 years, I decided to replace it with a brand new LG.
Comments (English): After my trusted Bosch dishwasher gave out after 22 years, I decided to replace it with a brand new LG. That was a massive mistake.Delivered at the end of October, the dishwasher died after just two weeks. When the first LG technician arrived, he spent less than three minutes in my house before lazily blaming a "voltage issue" and telling me to call an electrician. I did, which cost me out-of-pocket, and my electrician confirmed the wiring and voltage were absolutely perfect.After complaining about being misdiagnosed, LG assigned me a representative named John from the "Presidential Liaison" team. Rather than getting executive treatment, the service plummeted. John routinely ignores follow-ups and takes days to respond.Since then, a second technician found a broken control board. It took 5 business days to arrive and replace. The moment it was fixed and turned on? A brand new error code appeared: the heat sensor was also broken. Today, they ordered another part, meaning yet another 5-business-day wait.I understand that technology can occasionally fail out of the box. What I cannot accept is a company refusing to replace a clearly faulty, brand-new appliance, forcing the customer to endure endless repairs, and assigning a "liaison" who does nothing to manage the situation.I recently bought an LG washer and dryer as well, but this experience has completely ruined the brand for me. You learn the true quality of a company when things go wrong, and LG has failed miserably. Avoid their appliances, the customer care is nonexistent.

Sentence (English): HOW I LANDED ON THIS MODEL:-----------------------------------------------A Whirlpool Gold came with our house.
Comments (English): [ Cleans every time ] || ---------------- || HOW I LANDED ON THIS MODEL:-----------------------------------------------A Whirlpool Gold came with our house. I looked up the year that model was discontinued, and that was an impressive longevity without any known service. I assumed KitchenAid, being the higher end tier, would have similar quality and performance. After some research, I landed on this model. I am not disappointed.I compared this to two other major brands, and it was tough. Based on how I use the dishwasher, I felt the unique third rack design might win out slightly in that area. This model added a pop-open drying system, and is supposed to dry better than previous models.A competitor claims to have a built-in softener, but that requires regular cartridge replacements. A quick Google search claimed that to be a failure point for a small percentage. We have soft water. Why add something that I do not need? Another brand features steam and is slightly quieter. While the steam was enticing, I reflected on how well my 14(? ) year old Whirlpool cleaned. Shouldn't this new model be just as good or better? Even with the top rack arm option,and 44db is slightly quieter than my old dishwasher. Visitors frequently complimented that they didn't even realize the old unit was running. SO HOW DOES IT STAND UP? -----------------------------------------There are pros and cons over my old dishwasher. Some of the cons were overcome by making adjustments to how the unit is loaded. Concerns are not about cleaning; it's more about how to pack a full tub. It's a different layout with that third rack.PROS:---------1. In the 3 months of use, I have NOT had any dish come out with residue. (I mostly use "Pro Wash" to sense the amount of residue on my dishes.)2. Quiet! 3. Dries well. The standard dry cycle is usually all I need. Some competitors claim to dry plastics better. The only issue I've had is if an item has a place for water to pool on top of. I don't imagine any dishwasher can compensate for that scenario.4. Learning to use the top rack. (I have even run a couple cycles "Top 2 Racks" only.)CONS:----------1. I had to adjust how I thought about loading a dishwasher. It took me a while to get used to not being able to stack full-sized cups on the left side of my middle rack. (The top rack hangs lower.) However, I now place some cups on the top rack. I will share a little after the cons.2. If the middle rack is not at the highest setting, vertically stacked plates will obstruct the control arm. Even at the highest settings, I have some large serving plates that will still obstruct the arm. (I angle them to fix this issue.) This appears to be a limitation of having a more robust top rack.3. Wash cycles are longer than my older unit. After some research, it appears that all of the major brands have longer cycles, due to energy conservation efforts. This may be a con of all newer dishwashers, but I wanted to address it as something one may notice.4. I almost always push a control panel button when I try to open the door. The buttons are placed where it's natural to grab. This is not an issue, because nothing starts until a final selection is made. It's just something I noticed, and I've seen other reviewers note.FINAL THOUGHTS:---------------------------I waited to share this review, because I questioned whether the larger top rack was worth the perceived space constraints. In my case, I have cups that fit angled on the top rack, so this works in my situation. I am learning to appreciate this dishwasher more than regret it.If you do a lot of baking, it might be worthwhile to measure or take your favorite baking pans into the store. The top rack is great for cups, small containers, spatulas and light silverware loads. It first felt as if things didn't fit properly. I do have some cups that are too long to angle at the top.The left side of the middle rack does not have a high clearance, but I have been able to rearrange the way I load my dishwasher to compensate.The cleaning quality appears to be top notch, 44db is pretty quiet, and it does dry well.I am pleased with this model.
